items.followUp: State the steps of the head-to-tail rule and explain how to draw the resultant of two vectors.

rubric.why: Checks the required arrangement of successive vectors.
rubric.description: Places successive vectors head to tail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the tail of each successive vector is placed at the head of the previous vector.

rubric.why: Checks how the resultant is drawn after arranging the vectors.
rubric.description: Draws the resultant from the first vector’s tail to the last vector’s head.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.

modelAnswer: Place the tail of the second vector at the head of the first vector, and continue this for any further vectors.
The resultant is drawn from the tail of the first vector to the head of the last vector.

items.followUp: State the law of inertia and give two everyday examples of it.

rubric.why: Checks that the law includes the states of motion and the external force needed to change them.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by an external force.

rubric.why: Checks a correct example of inertia of motion.
rubric.description: Gives an example of passengers tending to move forward when a moving vehicle stops suddenly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as passengers tending to move forward when a bus stops suddenly.

rubric.why: Checks a correct example of inertia of rest.
rubric.description: Gives an example of passengers tending to move backward when a vehicle starts suddenly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as passengers tending to move backward when a bus starts suddenly.

modelAnswer: The law of inertia states that a body remains at rest or continues in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force.
When a moving bus stops suddenly, passengers tend to move forward.
When a bus starts suddenly, passengers tend to move backward.
